To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a methodology for the design of relational databases has been defined, and the methodology has been implemented in a software tool.

1) the extended entity-relationship diagram can be used to represent the conceptual design of a relational database, 2) the extended entity relationship model can be decomposed into a relational database schema using a set of basic transformations, and 3) a set of basic normalization transformations can be used to normalize the relational database schema.
the design process can be broken down into a set of basic steps, that the basic design steps can be automated to some degree, and that the design steps can be performed in a logical manner.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and evaluation of a methodology for the design of relational databases.
a methodology for designing large relational databases.
the development of a logical design methodology for relational databases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the methodology presented in this thesis is a logical design methodology for large relational databases, and is based on the use of the extended entity-relationship data model.
a logical database design methodology has been defined that is both complete and consistent.
this methodology provides a systematic approach for the design of high quality large relational databases.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the extended entity-relationship data model is a powerful and expressive data modeling tool that can be used to model a large variety of data requirements in a natural and intuitive manner, and the methodology presented here is effective in translating the conceptual design of the data requirements into a relational design.
we have developed a logical design method for relational databases that has been implemented in a computer-aided design system.
a methodology has been developed to design relational databases from conceptual specifications using the extended entity-relationship data model.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the extended entity-relationship modeling is very effective in conceptualizing data requirements.

the extended entity-relationship data model is a very useful tool for the conceptualization of data requirements and that the extended entity relationship model is an appropriate starting point for the logical design of large relational data-bases.
the design process is based on a set of basic transformations that are applied to the extended entity-relationship constructs.
